prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” roofing company that’s right for everyone — the best choice depends on your ZIP code, budget, roof material, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, and whether you want manufacturer-certified installers. I can help you find a great contractor, but first I recommend the approach below.

If you want me to shortlist specific companies near you, tell me your Dallas ZIP code and a few priorities (budget, fastest schedule, best warranty, insurance help, shingle vs. metal, etc.).

How to find the best roofing company for your replacement
1. Get at least 3 written estimates
   - Make sure each estimate lists scope (tear-off vs. overlay), materials (brand & product line), number of layers removed, underlayment, flashing, ventilation, ice & water shield, disposal, and permit fees.

2. Prefer manufacturer-certified installers
   - Look for GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, etc. Those certifications mean the company meets training and insurance standards and can offer better manufacturer warranties.

3. Verify insurance, licensing and local permits
   - Ask for a certificate of liability insurance and workers’ comp (or state-required proof). Confirm the company pulls required city/county permits and will schedule inspections.

4. Check reputation and references
   - Read Google/Yelp/Angi/Bing reviews, check the BBB, and ask for local references (recent jobs in Dallas). Look for consistent, recent positive feedback and fast responses to warranty or follow-up issues.

5. Ask about warranties & workmanship guarantees
   - Get both the manufacturer warranty (on shingles) and the contractor’s workmanship warranty in writing. Ask if warranties are transferable if you sell the home.

6. Clarify timeline and payment terms
   - Typical reasonable deposit is 10–30% with final payment upon completion and permit sign-off. Avoid contractors demanding large upfront cash payments.

7. Watch for red flags
   - Storm-chasers or contractors who pressure you for a quick decision, vague contracts, no local address, no insurance proof, or insistence on full cash payment.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Are you manufacturer-certified? Which brands/products do you install?
- Can you provide proof of liability insurance and local business registration?
- Do you pull the permits and handle inspections?
- Can you provide 3 local references and photos of recent Dallas jobs?
- What is covered in your workmanship warranty and how long does it last?
- What is the start date, expected duration, and payment schedule?
- Will you provide a written final lien waiver upon payment?

Want help next?
- If you give your ZIP code and priorities, I can suggest criteria-based options and draft an email/phone script you can use to request apples-to-apples quotes. I can also provide a comparison checklist template to evaluate estimates. Which would you like?
